relationship_basis_note: Carries the runtime flow (intent → lens/context → wiki lookup → selected inputs → create/update Working AIP → readiness check → aiws-aip run) for the handoff that this spec only summarizes in its v0.9.9 addendum; it is where an executor goes to actually move from discovery into AIP-guarded execution. It applies, and does not redefine, the AIP artifact model — no coupling with the §5 metadata/section schema here.

The Working AIP Connection addendum in this spec restates, in compressed form, a contract owned elsewhere: the mandatory-Working-AIP-before-non-trivial-execution rule, the minimum Working AIP section list, and the "support artifacts may feed but never replace" boundary. Coupling = that rule set + the minimum section list; if the readiness levels, minimum fields, or the anti-confusion table change in the connection spec, the addendum here goes stale.

Defines the NODES the edges here connect (node_kind object vs artifact, source_id identity, __OBJECT__ locator, DP5/INV-3 no-rollup); coupling = endpoint node_kind, which selects the permitted relation register and type (documentary / representation `represented_by` / domain `x:`) per §4 and §6A here against §3bis.6 there; a change to the node kinds or to the no-rollup invariant changes which relation types are legal on an edge.

The edges this spec defines are stored as bullets inside the `## Related Sources` block of an artifact meta, and that meta/index record model (2-layer: meta file + slim index.jsonl) is owned there; coupling = the section heading name, the bullet fields (SRC-id / role / basis / confidence) and the frontmatter keys the endpoints resolve against (source_id, node_kind, artifact_locator); a change to the meta schema or that block changes what build_relations.py can parse and what relations.jsonl can project.

The access capabilities resolve_object_or_concept / retrieve_object_profile / expand_from_object read the object-node meta defined here, and for an object node (artifact_locator=__OBJECT__, no file) inspect_source_anchor is redefined as following `represented_by` edges; coupling = node_kind, the __OBJECT__ sentinel and the three registers; a change to either breaks the capability contract that tool/RAG/MCP adapters map onto.

This spec is the node half of one model and defers the edge half to it: full semantics of the 3 registers and of the relationship roles live there; coupling = the relation-type registry and register-membership rules that an object node's `## Related Sources` out-edges must use (INV-4 requires at least one out-edge); a change to the register set or type registry changes which edges an object node may legally carry.

Routing resolves an object/concept to an object-node meta (node_kind=object) when one exists, else to the describing artifact metas, then expands over its `## Related Sources`; coupling = node_kind, source_id identity and the out-edge registers defined here; a change to object identity, kinds or the __OBJECT__ locator changes what routing can resolve and expand.

The §3bis.4 discovery hints consume `classification_signals` from the artifact-type taxonomy as the heuristic input for locating object candidates in real documents; coupling = that field's name and content per artifact_type; if the signals are renamed or re-scoped, the object-discovery hints stop resolving.

Object candidates are read out of the artifact-understanding output field `key_objects_and_terms`, which that schema owns; coupling = that output field; if the understanding output schema drops or renames it, the object-discovery pass loses its input record.

Object identity and findability are expressed with the key tiers owned there: official ID/name to T1, multilingual names to aliases, natural phrasing matched via T2/T3 (§3, §3bis.2 here); coupling = the tier definitions and the lookup_keys/aliases fields an object meta must populate; a change to tiering or key rules changes whether an object node (e.g. bare `F03` for SRC-FUNC-F03) is resolvable by ordinary lookup.

The §3bis.4 discovery hints consume `object_extraction_targets` from the knowledge profile — the per-artifact-type declaration of which objects to extract; coupling = that field as carried in profiles/*.yml; dropping or renaming it removes the input that drives object candidate proposals.

An object node is not a separate record: it is written as an ordinary source meta in the schema owned there and lands in the same slim index.jsonl; coupling = the frontmatter keys node_kind, source_id, artifact_locator (the __OBJECT__ sentinel, INV-9), lookup_keys/aliases, plus the index projection; a change to the meta frontmatter or index fields changes how object nodes are stored, linted and found.

Cited once, at the end, for the confirmed-vs-inferred provenance separation that routing output preserves when reporting evidence; vocabulary alignment only — routing reads no field this spec owns and no schema or data flows between them.

The T1/T2/T3 key tiers owned there are the match inputs a query is scored against during routing; coupling = the tier definitions and the lookup_keys field carried in artifact meta; a change to tiering or key-quality rules changes which sources route first and whether a query resolves at all.

Routing consumes the artifact-level meta (Lớp 1) whose structure is owned there — that meta plus the slim index.jsonl projection is the record routing matches, filters, scopes and stops on; coupling = the fields routing reads (lookup_keys, knowledge_targets, authority/freshness, meta_locator/artifact_locator); a change to those fields or to the index projection changes routing inputs and precedence outcomes.

The no-auto-promotion boundary these patches encode in tooling (refresh emits draft/candidate by default, apply is explicit + reviewed + logged, detect/evaluate emit signals not approvals — P0-03, P1-02, §10) is the draft/review/apply promotion state machine owned there; coupling = the promotion states and who may transition them; if the promotion model changes, the patched tool output wording and the lint boundary checks must change with it.

This guide is the patch/merge map for that spec's decisions: WTA-01..WTA-09 items are mapped here to concrete tool patches (P0/P1/P2) and to canonical merge destinations (§9 table); coupling = the WTA item set and its boundary statements (lookup = routing not verification; refresh = draft not promotion); if the spec's items or boundaries change, this patch map, its targets and its §7 compatibility checklist go stale.

Same-sprint companion: this guide states the intended patches, the merge summary records which of them actually landed in canonical (§8 lists both as canonical additions); coupling = the P0/P1 patch list and its merge status; the two carry complementary halves — planned patch vs merged outcome — of the same sprint record.

The optional meta fields the P0-04 patch adds to build_wiki_source_meta.py and the P1-01 patch projects into the index (authority_level, freshness_status, source_representation_status/caution, knowledge_value, intended_ai_use, promotion_status) are meta/index schema fields owned there; coupling = those field names and allowed values; a schema change invalidates the patch targets and the old-meta/new-meta compatibility checklist in §7.

The v0.9.11 addendum in this spec adopts the runtime-sanity rule ("before non-trivial execution, check Working AIP readiness") from the Minimal Runtime Testing stance, which decides what MVP runtime testing does and does not cover (deterministic guardrail + boundary checks; explicitly no scoring/telemetry/semantic review). Coupling = the scope of what is verified; widening or narrowing that stance changes what this spec's addendum is expected to assert.

The sanity checklists (sprint close / canonical merge / package close) contain the concrete check items that assert Working AIP boundary and readiness — they consume the readiness levels (§7), the readiness checklist (§8) and the aiws-aip run pre-execution checklist (§19) defined here. Coupling = the readiness field set; adding or dropping a readiness item here leaves the corresponding checkbox there out of date.

Defines the container that this spec's runtime file set lives in: what a Workspace is, the executor-agnostic Task Workspace at `.ai-work/workspaces/{account}/{task_id}/` (one workspace shared by AIP run / agent run / agent-via-AIP run), and the boundary against Working AIP, Knowledge Hub, Notebook and canonical docs. Coupling = workspace placement + the boundary statement this spec's addendum reproduces verbatim; a change to the Task Workspace path or to the boundary propagates into every placement path in §3–§14 here.

Carries the runtime flow for the artifacts this spec defines: when a Workspace is created, how the Runtime Queue and Capture Inbox are worked during execution, and the classify/close pass at task end. It consumes the file names and enums fixed here (`02_investigation_queue.jsonl` / `02_runtime_queue.jsonl`, `08_capture_inbox.jsonl`, capture status/target enums), so renaming or re-enumerating the file set here propagates to it.

§4.2 names the Wiki v1 freeze summary as a document this guide requires to be updated/annotated, so that it records that working and legacy sources share one source-side model and differ only by reading priority. It is an edit target, not a reference: the freeze summary's current wording is what determines whether that prescribed update is still outstanding or already applied.

The policy artifact this guide's Phase A tells you to install first; it fixes the vocabulary (`source_role=working|legacy`, `source_use_rule`, the working-over-legacy reading priority) that every update step here then propagates into the wiki/source contract, meta+index builders, lookup and lint. Coupling = that role/use-rule vocabulary; if the policy redefines or extends it, the field and lint updates prescribed in §4–§5 here change accordingly.

Package member listed by this manifest: the guide for updating an existing AI Work System installation (wiki/source contract, tooling, lint, wiki prompts) so it carries `source_role` / `source_use_rule` without redesign. The manifest carries the file list only; no data coupling beyond package membership.

Package member listed by this manifest: the project-side procedure for actually adding a working and a legacy source set into one project's wiki. The manifest carries the file list only; no data coupling beyond package membership.

Entry document of the Wiki Source Role package this manifest enumerates: it states the package purpose (bringing working and legacy sources into the Knowledge Hub) and its intended use, which the manifest itself does not carry. The manifest's file list and the README's `## Included` list describe the same package membership, so adding or removing a package file must move both.

Package member listed by this manifest and the normative layer of the package: it defines `source_role` (working|legacy), `source_use_rule` and the reading priority. The manifest carries the file list only — the rules themselves live there; no data coupling beyond package membership.

The system-side layer of the package this README fronts: it maps the package's second stated purpose ("update nhẹ design/spec/package hiện tại của AI Work System") onto the concrete places to change — wiki/source contract fields, tooling, lint, wiki prompts. Read when adapting an existing AIWS installation rather than a project's wiki.

The project-side layer of the package this README fronts: it carries the actual procedure for the README's third stated use ("hướng dẫn đưa 2 bộ source vào wiki của một dự án phần mềm"). Read when ingesting a working and a legacy source set into a concrete project wiki.

The policy layer of the package this README fronts: the README states only what the package is for, while `source_role=working|legacy`, `source_use_rule` and the working-vs-legacy reading priority are defined there. Anyone acting on the working/legacy distinction reads the policy; the README carries no rules of its own.

The baseline note only records WHICH AIP conventions entered the canonical baseline at v0.9.18 (retrospective AIP, slug prefix taxonomy, cross-AIP depends_on/related fields) and at which spec version; the normative rules and section numbering live in AIP_Detail_Spec_MVP. Coupling = the spec's section map (§3.5/§4.3/§5.3-5.7/§12.4) quoted here; when the spec re-sections or changes those rules, this note stays a point-in-time record and its delta summary goes stale — read the spec for the rule in force, the note only for when it entered the baseline.

The baseline note declares AIWS_Change_Request_Spec_MVP the general AIWS-wide CR authority as of the 2026-06-19 baseline (with WIKI_CHANGE_REQUEST_SPEC demoted to a wiki-meta profile), but carries none of the CR rules itself — mandatory fields, month-scoped/cross-branch CR-id allocation and the CR authoring conventions are all in that spec. Anyone resolving "which document governs a CR" gets the pointer here and the content there; if the spec's authority scope changes, this baseline declaration is what goes out of date.

README is the entry doc of the methodology package and defines its curated reading order; item 15 of that order is the source-role policy, which holds the actual working-source vs legacy-source classification rules for the project wiki / Knowledge Hub source-side model. README carries only the ordering plus a one-line zone description — no rules and no content coupling: a change to the policy's classification does not change README.

AIP_Sample_CreateChatConfirmRequirement is the mapped PLAN-phase counterpart of this EXEC preset: the EXEC's Required Inputs I-02/I-03/I-04/I-07 (grouped block-first open points, BrSE-confirmed input understandings, chat channel/receiver, expected answer types) are the outputs inherited from that PLAN, and its entry conditions assume they exist. Coupling = the PLAN's handoff output set; if the sample changes what PLAN produces, this EXEC's Required Inputs table and Workspace Preconditions no longer line up.

AIP_Sample_CreateMailConfirmRequirement is the mapped PLAN-phase counterpart of this EXEC preset: the mail EXEC consumes what that PLAN hands off — grouped open points by topic, expected answer types per point, current assumptions, downstream impact understanding, approved wording/tone direction and expected reply deadline — which appear as its Required Inputs I-01/I-02/I-08/I-10. Coupling = that inherited output set; a change to it invalidates this EXEC's entry conditions ("BrSE đã confirm input understandings").

The two presets partition the design task space: this one only authors a BD/DD/Screen Design, and its Out of Scope routes any review-of-someone-else's-design to AIP_EXEC_ReviewDesign. They share no inputs or outputs (no data coupling) — the dependency is preset selection: whoever must decide author-vs-review needs both scope boundaries, and if one preset's boundary moves the other's Out of Scope list must move with it.

STEP-04 of this preset (self-review of the design draft before the BrSE checkpoint) names AIP_REVIEW_CHECKLIST_v0_3 as its Applicable Guidelines — the checklist supplies the criteria set the draft design document is graded against at that quality gate. Coupling = that criteria set; if the checklist adds/removes criteria, the pass condition of this preset's self-review step changes with it.

AIP_Sample_RequirementHandoff_Offshore is the declared mapped PLAN sample for this EXEC preset; the EXEC only starts once the PLAN phase has settled the requirement scope and the ticket/output format ("format output đã chốt"), i.e. those confirmed items are the inputs it consumes to produce the Backlog Item + Req Summary + Confirmation Record. Coupling = the PLAN's output/format set; changing it shifts this EXEC's Required Inputs and the structure of the handoff artifacts.

Complementary half of the design task space: this preset only reviews an existing design and explicitly forbids creating one (and forbids editing the document under review — it outputs findings only), routing any authoring work to AIP_EXEC_CreateDesignDoc. No shared inputs or outputs; needed to pick the correct preset, and the two Out-of-Scope boundaries must stay mutually consistent.

AIP_Sample_ReviewDesign_Shared is the mapped PLAN-phase sample for this review EXEC: the EXEC's entry conditions require a PLAN (or equivalent) to have fixed the review scope/objective and BrSE-confirmed input understandings, and those are exactly what that PLAN sample produces and hands off. Coupling = the PLAN handoff set (review scope, confirmed understandings, downstream consumer of findings); if it changes, this EXEC's Workspace Preconditions and Mode A/B/C baseline assumptions no longer hold.

AIP_Sample_ReviewTestCase_Shared is the mapped PLAN-phase sample for this test-case review EXEC; the EXEC assumes the PLAN side has already fixed review scope and the confirmed input understandings it reads at STEP-00/STEP-01 (its intake form only backfills what PLAN did not supply). Coupling = the PLAN's handoff output set; a change there changes what this EXEC must intake from BrSE instead.

The two presets partition the test-case task space: this one only authors a new test case document (it does not execute tests and does not review someone else's), and both its Out of Scope and its Guidance route review work to AIP_EXEC_ReviewTestCase. No shared inputs/outputs — the dependency is choosing the right preset, and the two scope boundaries must remain complementary.

The EXEC preset executes the task this PLAN sample scopes, and consumes this doc's outputs: grouped open points (block-first), expected answer types per point, chat channel/receiver, approved tone direction. Coupling = the PLAN-to-EXEC handoff checklist and completion conditions here, which become the EXEC's entry conditions; a change to the EXEC's required inputs changes what this sample must hand off.

The EXEC preset executes the mail-confirm task this PLAN sample scopes, and consumes its outputs: grouped open points by topic, expected answer types, current assumptions pending reply, downstream impact, approved wording/tone, expected reply deadline. Coupling = the handoff checklist and completion conditions here, which become the EXEC's entry conditions; if the EXEC's required inputs change, this sample's handoff set must change with them.

This sample routes the design-doc task to the EXEC preset as the file to copy and fill (project / owner / plan_source, document type into Objective, paths into References to Read First, then STEP-00→STEP-05). Coupling = the STEP-00 scope decisions and Q&A answers from this sample flow into those preset fields; if the preset's fields or step range change, the fill instructions in §6 here go stale.

The EXEC preset executes the design review step-by-step and inherits this sample's outputs: confirmed input understandings, review scope (in/out), the 6 review dimensions and their priority, downstream context, project-specific checklist. Coupling = the handoff checklist and completion conditions here, which become the EXEC's entry conditions; a change to the EXEC's dimensions or entry conditions changes what this sample must produce.

Scope boundary between two presets: this sample covers CREATING test cases; reviewing someone else's test cases is explicitly out of its scope and routed to the ReviewTestCase EXEC preset instead. Routing pointer only — no field or content coupling between the two presets.

This sample routes the test-case task to the EXEC preset as the file to copy and fill (project / owner / plan_source, coverage level into Workspace Preconditions, paths into References to Read First, then STEP-00→STEP-05). Coupling = the coverage level and scope settled in this sample feed those preset fields; if the preset's fields or step range change, the fill instructions in §7 here go stale.

AIP_Detail_Spec_MVP defines the AIP schema (frontmatter fields, required sections per type, step structure) that any new AIP template or preset must satisfy; this guide declares it a required input for Case F (create a new AIP template / preset document). A schema change there changes what a conformant template produced under Case F must contain.

Case C (review a canonical artifact before publishing) declares this checklist a required input: it carries the 47 conformance criteria and the Minimum-tier pass/fail gate a reviewer walks and fills. Criteria added, retired or re-tiered there change the work a Case-C review task must perform.

Case C declares this guideline a required input alongside the checklist: it supplies the per-criterion Purpose / Anti-pattern / Spec reference used to judge pass/fail when a criterion is unclear. Its entries are keyed to the checklist's criterion IDs, so a renumbering there breaks lookup during a Case-C review.

This checklist declares AIP_Detail_Spec_MVP as its `authoritative_spec` and derives its structural criteria from that spec's §5/§6/§7.1/§10. Coupling = the spec's mandatory frontmatter fields, required-section counts per artifact type, step-field rules and its section numbering; if the spec adds, retires or renumbers any of those, the matching S-NN criteria here go stale or missing.

1:1 companion pair over the same criterion set: this file carries the criteria, tiers and verdict gate; the guideline carries the Purpose / Anti-pattern / Spec reference for the SAME S-NN / SM-NN IDs. Coupling = the criterion ID set — adding, retiring or renumbering a criterion in one file requires the matching edit in the other, otherwise a reviewer hits an orphan or a missing rationale entry.

This guideline declares AIP_Detail_Spec_MVP as its `authoritative_spec` and every criterion entry ends in a 'Spec ref' pointing into that spec's sections (§5.1, §5.2–§5.5, §6.2–§6.4, §7.4 …). Coupling = the spec's section numbering plus its field/section enums; a renumber or an enum change there invalidates the Spec-ref lines and the anti-pattern examples written here.

1:1 companion pair over the same criterion set: the checklist holds the criteria, tiers and pass/fail gate; this file holds the rationale for the SAME S-NN / SM-NN IDs and exists only to be looked up per criterion. Coupling = the criterion ID set — a criterion added, retired or renumbered in the checklist leaves a missing or orphan entry here.

The 'Design new spec' dependency reminder names AIP_Detail_Spec_MVP as the structure-compliance input for the AIP produced by that task. Coupling = the AIP schema (frontmatter, required sections, step structure) every PLAN/EXEC this table routes must satisfy; a schema change there moves the compliance bar for the mapped tasks.

The preset-task table routes the task 'Clarify requirements từ meeting transcript' straight to this EXEC preset file (standalone EXEC, output = RD / clarification document) — it is the only row naming a preset file rather than a folder. If that preset is renamed, moved or replaced, this row resolves to nothing.

This mapping table names preset FOLDERS (`aip_samples/design/`, `aip_exec/testcase/` …) and delegates the full file listing to PRESET_INDEX, which is the catalogue of preset_knowledge. Coupling = the preset library's file inventory: a reader must open the index to resolve a folder pointer here into an actual preset file, and newly added or renamed presets surface in the index first.

The 'Review canonical artifact' dependency reminder names this checklist a required input for the review task this table routes; it supplies the conformance criteria and the pass/fail gate that produce that row's 'Review findings' output. Criteria changes there change what the mapped review task must cover.

The 'Review canonical artifact' dependency reminder names this guideline a required input alongside the checklist; it supplies the per-criterion rationale (Purpose / Anti-pattern / Spec ref) used to decide pass/fail during the review task this table routes. Its entries are keyed to the checklist's criterion IDs.

The index routes the 'Candidate / CR / governance' goal to this spec as the AIWS-wide CR authority, with the wiki-local WIKI_CHANGE_REQUEST_SPEC listed directly above it as a profile of it. Coupling = the CR mandatory fields and approval flow a governance task must follow; if that authority moves or its required fields change, the governance path this index publishes points at the wrong contract.

PROJECT_WIKI_BUILDUP_GUIDELINE covers the first-build loop only and explicitly forbids re-running its steps for maintenance; the maintenance counterpart for the same metas/index (per-meta update, refresh, whole-repo sync) is WIKI_META_BUILD_UPDATE_GUIDELINE. Coupling = the meta field/slot contract and the candidate→review→apply gates both loops write against; every meta a build produces is subsequently governed by the update guideline, so a change to its update rules changes what a first build must leave behind.

The pre-apply gate of the meta update flow (Appendix A §7E) reads the Promotion trigger list (CR-D8) defined in Controlled_Knowledge_Promotion_Spec_MVP: if an update matches a trigger (set knowledge_class=source_of_truth, change a referenced source_id, split/merge metas, deprecate, change Related Sources between major artifacts) the lightweight update MUST stop and go through CR + wiki manager. Coupling = that trigger list; adding or removing a trigger there changes which meta edits may be applied directly.

Meta extraction is driven by the profile plus the Project Mapping Pattern (`pmp_<profile_id>.yml`, which takes precedence for extraction logic while the profile still supplies `knowledge_targets`); the PMP schema, its canonical path next to the profile, and the Profile-vs-PMP precedence rule are defined in WIKI_PROFILE_GENERATION_CUSTOMIZATION_GUIDELINE. Coupling = profile/PMP schema + precedence + file path; a change there changes what `build_wiki_source_meta.py` extracts into every meta built or refreshed under this guideline.

Profiles and PMPs authored under this guideline feed metas whose canonical slot vocabulary (ui_ux_behavior / api_contract / be_processing_logic ...) and split-meta FE/API/BE source-id convention are defined in WIKI_META_BUILD_UPDATE_GUIDELINE §18. Coupling = the slot names + split naming/`companion_design` linking rules the profile's slot-mapping tables must emit into; a slot renamed or re-scoped there invalidates the mapping tables configured here.

The PMP YAML schema defined here carries an `artifact_type` field whose allowed values are the enum owned by Artifact_Type_Taxonomy_Spec_MVP, and the profile/slot tables are keyed by the same artifact types. Coupling = the artifact_type enum; adding, renaming or retiring a type there changes which values profiles and PMPs may declare.

Every builder this routing table dispatches to must emit a meta in the schema owned there (frontmatter + Summary / Knowledge Targets / Lookup Keys, or a partial carrying `needs_completion`), while this spec's own _build_routing.json registry is explicitly NOT projected into index.jsonl (§3 invariant) and §A12 there was amended to sanction this spec; coupling = the meta record schema plus the index projection boundary; a change to the meta schema changes the build-tool contract and what lint_wiki will accept from a routed builder.
